newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lion to list on SES via suspended firm.
newsitem.headline: Lion to list on SES via suspended firm.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Lion Group said on Wednesday it planned to list its assets on the mainboard of the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) through Malaysian Feedmills Ltd (MFL).
Lion said in a statement MFL, a former producer of animal feed and agricultural products, was suspended from trading on the SES in June 1988 after several years of losses.
Lion, listed in Kuala Lumpur, planned to inject its assets into MFL and had received in-principle approval from the SES for the lifting of the trading suspension.
It said it wanted to restructure and rescue MFL, turning it into "a profitable and ongoing concern" thereby allowing existing shareholders an opportunity to recoup part of their investments.
Lion said it would inject its steel trading and property-based businesses into the new company, to be called, Lion Teck Chiang Ltd.
It said the proforma consolidated turnover of the new company would have been Singapore $115.75 million for the year ended June 30, 1995. Pre-tax profit would have been S$15.7 million, it said.
Under the rescue plan, the issued and paid-up capital of MFL would be reduced to S$1.5 million from S$15 million "to better reflect the available assets of MFL".

The issued and paid-up share capital would then be increased after the restructuring to S$71 million, comprising 142 million shares of S$0.50 each. Lion said it would propose a share offer of 32.52 million shares, comprising nine million new shares and 23.52 million vendor shares, through a restricted offer and a public offer.
A further 4.7 million shares would be sold privately to Bidara Holdings Sdn Bhd, a substantial shareholder of MFL.
MFL shareholders would be offered 12 million shares on the basis of four offer shares for every one share held.
"The public offer would comprise a total of 20.52 million shares, representing about 14.4 percent of the enlarged share capital of the restructured MFL," it said.
Up to 10 percent of the offer shares would be reserved for the management, staff and business associates of the restructured company.
"Following the restructuring and share offer, the Lion group will emerge as the controlling shareholder with 71.1 percent," it said.
"The price of the offer shares would be detemined at a later date, it said.
An extraordinary general meeting of shareholders would be held on December 19, 1996 to seek approval for the proposal, the statement added.
